title: Um apólogo
author: Machado de Assis
blurb: A needle and a thread argue about which of them matters more. Two pages.
note: Published in 1885 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Johannes Vermeer, The Lacemaker, about 1669–70. Musée du Louvre, Paris. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Missa do galo
author: Machado de Assis
blurb: A young man waits up on Christmas Eve and talks with an older woman. He never quite understands the conversation.
note: Published in 1894 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Almeida Júnior, Reading, 1892. Pinacoteca de São Paulo. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Fábulas de Narizinho
author: Monteiro Lobato
blurb: Twenty-nine short fables from Aesop, La Fontaine and Brazilian folklore, retold for children with Brazilian animals. Most are a page or two.
note: Published in 1921, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931); the author died in 1948, so it is also in the public domain in Brazil, Portugal and the EU. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Maria Sibylla Merian, cicadas and lantern flies on a pomegranate branch, plate 49 of Metamorphosis insectorum Surinamensium, 1705. Koninklijke Bibliotheek, The Hague. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Contos para a infância (seleção)
author: Guerra Junqueiro
blurb: Seventeen fairy tales and short stories, among them Snow White, Little Red Riding Hood and the Steadfast Tin Soldier, retold in Portuguese for children.
note: Published in 1877; Guerra Junqueiro, who chose and retold the stories, died in 1923, and Andersen, the Grimms and his other authors long before, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Walter Crane, Little Red Riding Hood picking flowers in the wood, from his picture book Little Red Riding Hood, 1875. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Era uma vez...
author: Júlia Lopes de Almeida
blurb: A spoiled princess whose father has never told her no meets three blind men who seem to see more than she does. A fairy tale.
note: Published in 1917 and the author died in 1934, so it is in the public domain in the US and nearly everywhere else. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Edward Burne-Jones, Princess Sabra (The King’s Daughter), 1865. Musée d’Orsay, Paris. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: A cartomante
author: Machado de Assis
blurb: A woman visits a fortune teller about her lover, and the answer she gets makes him laugh at her.
note: Published in 1884 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Caravaggio, The Fortune Teller, about 1594. Capitoline Museums, Rome. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: O alienista
author: Machado de Assis
blurb: A doctor opens an asylum in a small Brazilian town and decides that nearly everyone belongs in it.
note: Published in 1882 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is the 19th-century original.
coverCredit: Tony Robert-Fleury, Pinel Freeing the Insane at the Salpêtrière, 1876. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: O mandarim
author: Eça de Queirós
blurb: A poor Lisbon clerk rings a little bell, a mandarin dies in China, and the clerk inherits his millions. Then his conscience follows him.
note: Published in 1880 and the author died in 1900, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Weng Pu, Portrait of a Young Official, 1751. National Museum, Warsaw. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Cinco minutos
author: José de Alencar
blurb: A young man misses the omnibus by five minutes, rides the next one beside a veiled stranger, and follows her as far as Europe. Told in a letter.
note: Published in 1856 and the author died in 1877, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is that of an 1894 edition.
coverCredit: Alexander Roslin, The Lady with the Veil (the Artist’s Wife), 1768. Nationalmuseum, Stockholm. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Iracema
author: José de Alencar
blurb: A poetic love story between an Indigenous woman of the Ceará coast and a Portuguese soldier.
note: Published in 1865 and the author died in 1877, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is that of an 1890 edition.
coverCredit: Frans Post, View of Olinda, Brazil, 1662. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Dom Casmurro
author: Machado de Assis
blurb: An older man writes down his life and tries to prove that his wife was unfaithful.
note: Published in 1899 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Belmiro de Almeida, The Quarrel (Arrufos), 1887. Museu Nacional de Belas Artes, Rio de Janeiro. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Memórias póstumas de Brás Cubas
author: Machado de Assis
blurb: A dead man tells his own life story, with jokes, in very short chapters.
note: Published in 1881 and the author died in 1908, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Almeida Júnior, Longing (Saudade), 1899. Pinacoteca de São Paulo. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Os Maias
author: Eça de Queirós
blurb: Three generations of a wealthy Lisbon family and a love affair that turns out to be a tragedy. A very long novel.
note: Published in 1888 and the author died in 1900, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Columbano Bordalo Pinheiro, The Grey Glove, 1881. Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea, Lisbon. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Amor de perdição
author: Camilo Castelo Branco
blurb: Two young people from feuding families fall in love in Viseu, and it leads to prison, a convent and exile. Portugal’s Romeo and Juliet.
note: Published in 1862 and the author died in 1890, so it is in the public domain worldwide. The spelling is the original.
coverCredit: Frank Dicksee, Romeo and Juliet, 1884. Southampton City Art Gallery. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
